newsitem.title: INDIA: Truckers end strike in Bombay, west Indian state.
newsitem.headline: Truckers end strike in Bombay, west Indian state.

text.p: A 10-day old truckers' strike was called off in the western state of Maharashtra, an official of the Bombay Port Trust said on Thursday.
"Our traffic manager was told the strike was off," the official said. Maharashtra is India's most industrialised state and its capital Bombay is the country's busiest port.
Truck operators in Maharashtra remained off the roads even after the strike was called off at the national level on Wednesday night.
The strike was called off after the state government's accepted most of the demands of truck operators, the Press Trust of India (PTI) news agency said.
Their demands included reduction in taxes and abolition of border check posts within three months.
Officials of Maharashtra Rajya Truck Tempo Tankers Bus Mahasangh, which represnts 180 unions, were not immediately available for comment.
India's truck operators had launched a nationwide strike to protest against the service tax and insurance premium hike proposed by the finance minister in his February 28 budget.
Truckers in Maharashtra continued their strike to force the state government to scrap some local taxes.
